headings.budget_meta: what the sector is required to place
headings.markers_meta: what the map can tell you before you jump

generation.order: Lines are filled in this order, and the map holds at most {grid} beacons ({grid_min}–{grid} by the community wiki's count). When they run out, generation stops — a line near the bottom can receive nothing at all.
generation.exhaust: This sector allocates up to {max} slots against {grid} beacons, so the bottom of the table is a wish list rather than a promise.
generation.at_risk: Could be cut entirely if everything above rolls high: {names}.
generation.nebula: Placed before everything else, whatever the file order, because the cloud graphics come first: {names}. A cloud drawn over an ordinary beacon converts it, and that beacon draws from the shared NEBULA list instead.
generation.fallback: Beacons still empty at the end of the table are filled from the shared {list} list ({ae} under Advanced Edition).
generation.exit: The exit beacon is not in this table at all — it draws from the shared {list}, and an exit inside a cloud is always empty.
generation.source: Generation rules per the community's reverse-engineering of the map generator; the game files state none of them.
generation.always_short: Cannot be filled even in the best case — the minima above it already use up the map: {names}.
generation.cannot_meet_minimum: This sector's minimum allocation is {min} against {grid} beacons, so it can never place everything it asks for.

markers.distress: Events here that carry the distress tag, so the beacon shows a distress marker. The map only draws distress and store markers on beacons adjacent to you, so this is a next-jump signal, not a plan for the sector:
markers.outside: Drawn from other lists but still carrying the distress tag, so they show the marker too — which is how a sector can show more distress beacons than its distress count: {names}.
markers.unmarked: The reverse case: allocated from the distress list but carrying no distress tag, so they do not show the marker — {names}.
markers.store: Events that open a store. A store beacon is marked only once you are within one jump of it, and an event that opens a shop as a reward is not marked at all until you arrive:
markers.scanners: Long-Ranged Scanners add a hazard reading and a possible-ship reading, still only for adjacent beacons. They never name the event, and a no-ship reading can still be a fight.
markers.outside_earlier: They are also filled before the distress line, so they take their beacons first. This is the case Fandom uses as its worked example.
markers.outside_later: They are filled after the distress line, so they add markers on top of it rather than competing with it for beacons.

special.label: Named beacons
special.hint: placed by name, not drawn from a pool

hostile.label: Hostile
hostile.hint: combat unless the row says otherwise

quests.label: Quest starts
quests.hint: marks a beacon elsewhere on the map

delta.head: Advanced Edition also defines {list}
delta.unconfirmed: Whether the engine substitutes this list for {name} is not stated by any file here.

rarity.note: Lower number = more common. A crew type at 0 is not sold in this sector's stores.

budget.legend: Solid blocks are the minimum the sector must place; faded blocks are the optional extra.
budget.zero: allocated 0–0 — the sector reserves the list but places none.
budget.expand: Open a line to see every event it can place; open an event to read its card here.

footnotes.unique: "Unique" is the files' own unique="true". Whether that means once per sector or once per run is not stated in any file here; the wiki's better bet is once per sector.
footnotes.unweighted: The shipped event lists carry no weights, so no beacon here has stated odds. A pool entry listed twice is counted as ×2 and marked.
footnotes.ambiguous: Defined in the files both as an event list and as a single event, and read here as the list: {names}.
footnotes.anonymous: {count} outcome(s) in these lists are written inline with no event id of their own, so they have no row here.
footnotes.no_card: No event tree was found for {names}, so those rows carry no tags.
footnotes.min_sector: minSector in the files is zero-indexed, so the "earliest sector" chip is that value plus one — the number a player counts from the start of a run. The community wiki states the same offset.
footnotes.floor: The 24-beacon ceiling follows from the 6×4 grid; the 19-beacon floor is stated by the community wiki alone and is not derivable from anything else here, so the at-risk marks use the ceiling.

cards.failed: Card unavailable — build it with tools/build-card.py, and open this page from disk.
